    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:

class BytesIOCopy:
    """A binary stream, backed by a real (temporary) file, whose contents
    are also copied to another stream as they are written.

    Being backed by a real file means this has a valid file descriptor,
    so it can be used as ``stdout``/``stderr`` for things like
    :func:`subprocess.run`, unlike a plain ``io.BytesIO``.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2

    .. versionchanged:: 8.3.1
        Backed by a temporary file instead of an in-memory buffer so it
        has a valid file descriptor.
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        self._file: t.BinaryIO = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._file, name)

    def flush(self) -> None:
        self._file.flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return self._file.write(b)

    def getvalue(self) -> bytes:
        pos = self._file.tell()
        self._file.seek(0)
        data = self._file.read()
        self._file.seek(pos)
        return data
